name: CPI (Industrial Workers)
sourceName: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment
remarks: Lag placeholder - last working day of subsequent month. One workbook stacks four base-year tables; the parser locates each block by its banner. None of the three older bases overlap the next one on any date, so splice_bases() had no data to estimate a rescale ratio from and was silently dropping all three (spliced=False) -- only the 2016-base segment (Sep 2020 onward) was ever reaching the frontend. Fixed with Labour Bureau's own published linking factors, confirmed against primary sources: 2016=100 to 2001=100 is 2.88 (PIB press release PRID=1666782, 22-Oct-2020 -- DG Labour Bureau's own words: "linking factor for the conversion of new series index to previous series on base 2001=100 is 2.88", i.e. 2001_value = 2016_value * 2.88, so this project's factor -- which expresses an OLDER base in the NEXT NEWER base's units -- is 1/2.88 on the 2001 entry); 1982=100 to 2001=100 is 4.63 (1982_value = 2001_value * 4.63, so 1/4.63 on the 1982 entry); 1960=100 to 1982=100 is 4.93 (1960_value = 1982_value * 4.93, so 1/4.93 on the 1960 entry).

The T-Bill side is weekly and the G-Sec side is a month-end snapshot, so the T-Bill series is resampled to ITS OWN month-end value (last auction on or before month-end) before subtracting -- not a monthly average, which would blend a different concept (typical yield during the month) into a spread that's otherwise a point-in-time reading on both legs.

name: Agricultural Wages
sourceName: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment
remarks: Headline = average 'Men' wage across the individual farm tasks, All-India, Agriculture occupation only (the newer files also carry Non-Agriculture rows, excluded). The source's year label is a JULY-JUNE agricultural year; the parser now dates it that way (it used to date it April-March, which put April-June readings a year early). Labour Bureau changed the task list and survey in 2013-14, so there are two bases: 1998-99 (11 tasks, Jul 1998 - Oct 2013) and 2013-14 (11 of the 12 new tasks, Nov 2013 onwards; 'Fishermen- coastal/deep-sea' is left out because it is blank in 24 months and would change the basket's composition). The two do not overlap and Labour Bureau publishes no linking factor, so link_factor 1.157 is OUR ESTIMATE (median of eight monthly ratios, Nov 2013 - Jun 2014, of the new-basket wage to the old basket's Oct 2013 wage moved forward by its own average seasonal change over the prior 8 years; individual months range 1.12-1.21). It only sets the level of the pre-Nov-2013 history in the spliced series; year-on-year rates for Nov 2013 - Oct 2014 inherit its uncertainty (roughly +/-4%). Months with fewer than 11 tasks reporting are dropped. Source gaps: Apr 2020 and Jul-Dec 2022.

name: Central Government Capital Expenditure
remarks: Old Tab/New Tab in the same file are two segments of one continuous series, not a rebasing -- but their column layouts differ: Old Tab has an extra blank column after "1.2 Non-Tax Revenue, Actual" that New Tab does not, shifting every later column one position right. Column 29/30 = "5 Capital Expenditure, Actual" (verified against the file's own header row); a prior version of this entry used column 29 for both sheets, which on Old Tab actually reads "4.1 Interest Payments, Revised Estimates" -- wrong line item AND wrong estimate type. RBI's own notes on this table say figures are cumulative during the financial year (April-March), not a monthly flow -- confirmed directly: values ramp up each month and reset low every April (e.g. this series peaks near Rs 10.7 lakh crore in March, then drops to ~Rs 1.9 lakh crore in April). YoY comparison of the same calendar month's cumulative figure (this series' `transform: yoy`) is the correct way to read this, not a month-over-month comparison, which would show the seasonal reset as a fake collapse.
